The '''Delsarte–Goethals code''' is a type of [[error-correcting code]].

== History ==

The concept was introduced by mathematicians Philippe Delsarte and J.-M. Goethals in their published paper.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.encyclopediaofmath.org/index.php/Delsarte-Goethals_code|title=Delsarte-Goethals code - Encyclopedia of Mathematics|website=www.encyclopediaofmath.org|language=en|access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Abhyankar |first1=S. == Function ==

The Delsarte–Goethals code DG(''m'',''r'') for even ''m'' ≥ 4 and 0 ≤ ''r'' ≤ ''m''/2&nbsp;−&nbsp;1 is a binary, [[non-linear code]] of length <math>2^{m}</math>, size <math>2^{r(m-1)+2m}</math> and [[Block code#The distance d|minimum distance]] <math>2^{m-1} - 2^{m/2-1+r}</math>

The code sits between the [[Kerdock code]] and the second-order [[Reed–Muller code]]s. More precisely, we have

: <math>K(m) \subseteq DG(m,r) \subseteq RM(2,m)</math>

When ''r'' = 0, we have DG(''m'',''r'') = ''K''(''m'') and when ''r'' = ''m''/2&nbsp;−&nbsp;1 we have DG(''m'',''r'') = RM(2,''m'').

For ''r'' = ''m''/2&nbsp;−&nbsp;1 the Delsarte–Goethals code has strength 7 and is therefore an [[orthogonal array]] OA(<math>2^{3m-1}, 2^m, \mathbb{Z}_2, 7)</math>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://mint.sbg.ac.at/desc_CDelsarteGoethals.html|title=MinT - Delsarte–Goethals Codes|last=Schürer|first=Rudolf|website=mint.sbg.ac.at|access-date=2017-05-22}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Abhyankar |first1=S.
